mainTopic: The trial of יואב before שלמה, and אגדות about יואב, אבנר and עמשא that close פרק נגמר הדין.
overview: The amud opens by closing the earlier topic with a short saying: better to be cursed than to curse. Then שלמה puts יואב on trial. יואב defends killing אבנר by saying אבנר should have stopped the רודף עשאל by wounding a limb, and he proves that אבנר could aim precisely. On the killing of עמשא, שלמה rejects יואב's claim that עמשא was a מורד במלכות. עמשא learned from the word רק that a king's order does not override Torah learning. שלמה then turns the charge around: יואב himself rebelled by following אדוניה, and he held back from following אבשלום only because דוד was still strong. רבי אבא בר כהנא disagrees, picturing דוד and יואב as partners who needed each other. The גמרא then explains פסוקים about how יואב judged and killed אבנר, why אבנר and עמשא were better and more righteous than יואב, and how generous and clean יואב's home was. The amud ends with the הדרן closing פרק נגמר הדין.

steps.title: Better to be cursed than to curse
steps.stepSummary: A short saying closes the earlier discussion about curses: better to be the one cursed than the one who curses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Be the one who is cursed, and not the one who curses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the previous discussion with a short saying: it is better to be the one who gets cursed than the one who does the cursing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line looks back at the curses discussed just before it. The idea is that a curse can come back to hurt the person who said it. So it is safer to be on the receiving end.
steps.whatToRemember: This saying closes the earlier topic. The next line returns to the story of יואב.

phrases.english: Be the one who is cursed,
and do not be the one who curses.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּהֵא לוּטָא, וְלָא תְּהֵא לָאטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A curse can come back to the one who says it, so it is better to be cursed than to curse.

steps.title: יואב is brought to trial and asked about אבנר
steps.stepSummary: יואב is brought before שלמה for judgment, and שלמה asks why he killed אבנר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought יואב, and he judged him. He said to him: What is the reason you killed אבנר?
steps.whatsHappening: The trial of יואב begins. שלמה asks him why he killed אבנר, which sets up the back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question opens the whole trial. יואב must give a legal reason why killing אבנר was not murder.

phrases.english: They brought Joab, and he judged him.
phrases.notes: The one judging is שלמה המלך.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is the reason
that you killed Abner?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא קְטַלְתֵּיהּ לְאַבְנֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story of יואב after the saying about curses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What legal reason did יואב have for killing אבנר?

steps.title: יואב says he was עשאל's blood avenger
steps.stepSummary: יואב answers that he was the גואל הדם of his brother עשאל, whom אבנר had killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I was the blood avenger of עשאל.
steps.whatsHappening: יואב defends himself. He says he killed אבנר as the גואל הדם for his brother עשאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גואל הדם may kill the person who killed his relative. יואב argues that this rule allowed him to kill אבנר.

keyTerms.meaning: blood avenger, a close relative who avenges a killing

phrases.english: He said to him: The blood avenger
of Asahel I was.
phrases.notes: עשאל was יואב's brother, and אבנר had killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גּוֹאֵל הַדָּם דַּעֲשָׂאֵל הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שלמה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יואב acted as עשאל's גואל הדם.

steps.title: But עשאל was a pursuer
steps.stepSummary: שלמה objects that עשאל was a רודף, so אבנר was allowed to kill him.
steps.simpleTranslation: עשאל was a pursuer.
steps.whatsHappening: שלמה pushes back. Since עשאל was chasing אבנר to kill him, אבנר killed him in self-defense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may kill a רודף to save himself. If אבנר's killing was allowed, then there was nothing to avenge, and the right of a גואל הדם does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: a pursuer trying to kill someone

phrases.english: Asahel was a pursuer.
phrases.notes: שלמה is speaking here, even though the text does not say 'he said to him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשָׂאֵל רוֹדֵף הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges יואב's גואל הדם defense.
steps.kashyaTarget: יואב's claim that he could kill אבנר as a גואל הדם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Killing a רודף is allowed, so אבנר was not a murderer. A גואל הדם has no right to avenge a killing that was allowed.

steps.title: אבנר could have stopped him by wounding a limb
steps.stepSummary: יואב answers that אבנר should have saved himself by hurting one of עשאל's limbs instead of killing him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He should have saved himself by striking one of his limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: יואב defends his position. He says that killing a רודף is allowed only when there is no gentler way to stop him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wounding the רודף would have been enough, killing him counts as murder. So יואב argues that אבנר was a murderer after all, and the rights of a גואל הדם apply again.

keyTerms.meaning: to save him (here, to save himself)
by striking one of his limbs

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses a basic rule of רודף: you may not kill him if wounding him would be enough to stop him.

phrases.english: He said to him: He should have saved himself
phrases.notes: Literally 'to save him.' It means אבנר should have saved himself.

phrases.english: by striking one of his limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָיָה לוֹ לְהַצִּילוֹ בְּאֶחָד מֵאֵבָרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רודף objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows when killing a רודף is allowed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since עשאל was a רודף, אבנר was allowed to kill him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Killing a רודף is allowed only when wounding him would not work, so אבנר was guilty.

steps.title: אבנר could not aim at a limb
steps.stepSummary: שלמה answers that אבנר was not able to aim at a limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He was not able to do that to him.
steps.whatsHappening: שלמה rejects יואב's answer. He says אבנר could not hit one of עשאל's limbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it was impossible to wound עשאל without killing him, then the rule from the last step does not apply. In that case אבנר was allowed to kill him.

keyTerms.meaning: he was not able to (do it to) him

phrases.english: He said to him: He was not able to do it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא יְכֵיל לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects יואב's claim that אבנר could have wounded a limb.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes אבנר could aim at a limb, but he could not.

steps.title: Proof that אבנר had precise aim
steps.stepSummary: יואב proves from a פסוק, as explained by רבי יוחנן, that אבנר hit עשאל exactly at the fifth rib. So he could have aimed at a limb too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Now, he aimed at him exactly at the fifth rib, as it is written: 'And אבנר struck him with the back end of the spear at the חומש.' And רבי יוחנן said: at the fifth rib, the place where the gallbladder and liver hang. Could he not aim at one of his limbs?
steps.whatsHappening: יואב brings a proof from the פסוק that אבנר struck an exact spot on עשאל's body. If he could aim that well, he could have hit a limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן explains that 'החומש' means the fifth rib, a very exact spot. Someone who can hit that spot can surely hit an arm or a leg. This knocks down שלמה's claim that אבנר could not aim.

keyTerms.meaning: now (here: 'if he could do this much')
the word in the פסוק that רבי יוחנן reads as 'fifth (rib)'

steps.whatToRemember: יואב wins the argument about אבנר. אבנר could aim, so he should have wounded עשאל instead of killing him.

phrases.english: He said to him: Now,
he aimed at him exactly at the fifth rib,
as it is written: 'And Abner struck him'
'with the back end of the spear at the ḥomesh,'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 2:23

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yoḥanan said: at the fifth rib,
the place where the gallbladder and liver hang.
Could he not hit him in one of his limbs?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא בְּדוֹפֶן חֲמִישִׁית כַּיוֵּן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disproves שלמה's claim that אבנר could not aim.
steps.raayaObject: That אבנר was able to aim precisely, so he could have wounded עשאל instead of killing him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 2:23, as explained by רבי יוחנן: 'החומש' means the fifth rib.

steps.title: Leave אבנר aside: why did you kill עמשא?
steps.stepSummary: שלמה accepts יואב's defense about אבנר and asks why he killed עמשא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Let אבנר go. What is the reason you killed עמשא?
steps.whatsHappening: שלמה drops the case of אבנר and opens a new charge, the killing of עמשא. This sets up יואב's next defense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Let אבנר go' means שלמה accepts that יואב had a good legal argument there. The trial now moves to a second killing that needs its own reason.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let Abner go,
what is the reason you killed Amasa?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נֵיזִיל אַבְנֵר, מַאי טַעְמָא קְטַלְתֵּיהּ לַעֲמָשָׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the outcome about אבנר and moves to a new charge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What legal reason did יואב have for killing עמשא?

steps.title: עמשא rebelled against the king
steps.stepSummary: יואב answers that עמשא was a מורד במלכות, because he came late after the king set him a deadline.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: עמשא was a rebel against the kingdom, as it is written: 'And the king said to עמשא: Gather for me the men of יהודה within three days... And עמשא went to gather יהודה, but he was late...'
steps.whatsHappening: יואב defends himself. He says עמשא rebelled against the king, and he proves it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד gave עמשא three days to gather the army, and עמשא came late. יואב argues that missing the king's deadline makes him a מורד במלכות, who deserves to die.

phrases.english: He said to him: Amasa
was a rebel against the kingdom,
as it is written: 'And the king said to Amasa:'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 20:4–5

phrases.english: 'Gather for me the men of Judah'
'within three days, etc.'
'And Amasa went to gather Judah,'
'and he was late, etc.'
phrases.notes: He came after the three-day deadline the king had given him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עֲמָשָׂא מוֹרֵד בַּמַּלְכוּת הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שלמה's question about עמשא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עמשא was a מורד במלכות because he missed the king's deadline, as the פסוק shows.

steps.title: עמשא limited the king's power through a דרשה
steps.stepSummary: שלמה rejects יואב's claim that עמשא was a מורד במלכות. עמשא explained the words אך and רק as limits on the king's authority.
steps.simpleTranslation: שלמה said to יואב: עמשא learned a limit on the king's power from the words 'אך' and 'רק'.
steps.whatsHappening: שלמה pushes back on יואב's answer from Step 9. He says עמשא had a Torah-based reason for coming late, so he was not a rebel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, יואב said עמשא deserved death because he ignored the king's deadline. שלמה answers that עמשא learned from limiting words in the פסוק that the king's power has limits. Someone who acts on a proper דרשה is not rebelling. The next step explains which דרשה he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The words אך and רק ('only'), which the Torah uses to limit or exclude something
He explained a פסוק and learned a rule from it
Commander of דוד's army whom יואב killed

phrases.english: He said to him: Amasa
phrases.notes: Here שלמה is the one speaking to יואב.

phrases.english: explained the words 'akh' and 'rak'.
phrases.notes: These are small words meaning 'only'. Wherever they appear, they are read as narrowing a rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עֲמָשָׂא אַכִּין וְרַקִּין דְּרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects יואב's claim in Step 9 that עמשא was a מורד במלכות
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that עמשא's delay counted as rebellion
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: יואב ignored that the king's authority has limits, and עמשא acted within those limits based on a דרשה

steps.title: Torah learning comes before the king's order
steps.stepSummary: עמשא found the men learning a tractate. From the word רק in יהושע 1:18, he learned that the king's order does not override Torah learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: עמשא found the men starting a tractate. He reasoned: the פסוק says anyone who rebels against the king's command shall die. You might think this applies even when the order would stop Torah learning. That is why the פסוק adds 'Only (רק) be strong and courageous', to limit the king's power.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the story and the drasha behind עמשא's delay. This shows why he was not a rebel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יהושע gives the king very wide power: whoever disobeys him is put to death. The word רק narrows that power, so it does not reach a case where obeying would stop people from learning Torah. Because the men had just started a tractate, עמשא was allowed to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: A tractate, a section of Torah learning
'One might think': introduces a mistaken idea that the next words will correct
'The פסוק teaches': introduces the words that prove the point

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the rule that a king's order does not override דברי תורה.

phrases.english: He found them starting a tractate.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the men of יהודה whom עמשא was sent to gather.

phrases.english: He said: It is written
"Any man who rebels against your command
and will not listen to your words
in all that you command him, shall be put to death."
phrases.notes: יהושע 1:18

phrases.english: One might think: even regarding words of Torah?
The verse teaches: "Only be strong and courageous."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק. The word רק ('only') is the limit עמשא relied on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ דִּפְתִיחַ לְהוּ בְּמַסֶּכְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and proves the דרשה mentioned in Step 10
steps.raayaObject: עמשא's delay was justified and was not rebellion
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word רק in יהושע 1:18, which limits the king's authority when it would stop Torah learning

steps.title: שלמה says יואב himself was the rebel
steps.stepSummary: שלמה turns the charge around: יואב himself was the מורד במלכות, because he followed אדוניה against the rightful king.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you (יואב) were the rebel against the kingdom, as the פסוק says: 'The news came to יואב, for יואב had followed אדוניה, though he had not followed אבשלום.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now שלמה goes on the attack. He says it is יואב, not עמשא, who rebelled against the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יואב had tried to justify his killings by calling his victims rebels. שלמה answers that יואב is guilty of exactly that crime, because he backed אדוניה instead of the rightful king. The פסוק also mentions that יואב did not follow אבשלום, and the גמרא will ask about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That man': a polite way of saying 'you'
Son of דוד who tried to take the throne instead of שלמה

phrases.english: Rather, that man
phrases.notes: שלמה means יואב himself. 'That man' is a polite way to avoid saying 'you'.

phrases.english: was a rebel against the kingdom,
as it is written: "And the news came to Joab,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 2:28

phrases.english: for Joab had turned after Adonijah
but after Absalom he did not turn."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָהוּא גַּבְרָא מוֹרֵד בַּמַּלְכוּת הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After clearing עמשא, שלמה turns the rebel charge back on יואב
steps.kashyaTarget: יואב's whole defense, which rests on the claim that he only killed rebels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יואב himself sided with אדוניה against the rightful king, so he is the real מורד במלכות

steps.title: What does 'he did not follow אבשלום' teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק needs to say that יואב did not follow אבשלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he did not turn' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about an extra detail in the פסוק. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about יואב following אדוניה, so there seems to be no reason to mention אבשלום. The גמרא assumes this extra detail must be teaching something.

keyTerms.meaning: What, or what does it mean?
Son of דוד who rebelled against his father

phrases.english: What does "he did not turn" mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לֹא נָטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the end of the פסוק quoted in Step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק mentions that יואב did not follow אבשלום

steps.title: יואב wanted to follow אבשלום but held back
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that יואב wanted to follow אבשלום but did not actually do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: He wanted to turn after אבשלום, but he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question from Step 13. The words 'he did not turn' tell us that יואב wanted to, but held back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words show that יואב was inclined to rebel even in אבשלום's time. This supports שלמה's picture of יואב as someone ready to rebel against the king.

keyTerms.meaning: He wanted to turn after (to side with)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
That he wanted to turn, but did not turn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ לִנְטוֹת וְלֹא נָטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that יואב wanted to follow אבשלום but did not actually do so

steps.title: Why did יואב hold back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if יואב wanted to follow אבשלום, why didn't he?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason he did not turn?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know יואב wanted to join אבשלום, the גמרא asks what stopped him. It is setting up רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's answer raises a new question. If יואב really wanted to rebel then, something must have held him back.

phrases.english: And what is the reason he did not turn?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא לָא נָטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on רב יהודה's answer in Step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What stopped יואב from following אבשלום even though he wanted to

steps.title: דוד was still strong
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that דוד was still full of strength back then, so יואב was afraid to join אבשלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: דוד's freshness (his strength) was still there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers that יואב held back only because דוד was still strong at the time of אבשלום's revolt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יואב held back out of fear, not loyalty. When דוד grew old and אדוניה rose up, יואב did join the rebellion. This backs up שלמה's charge that יואב was the real מורד במלכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'moisture'; here it means vitality and strength

steps.whatToRemember: שלמה cleared עמשא, because the word רק teaches that a king cannot stop Torah learning. He then showed that יואב was the real rebel: he wanted to join אבשלום, held back only out of fear of דוד, and later did follow אדוניה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
David's freshness was still present.
phrases.notes: Literally 'moisture'. It means דוד was still young and strong, so יואב was afraid of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: עֲדַיִין לִיחְלוּחִית שֶׁל דָּוִד קַיֶּימֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יואב held back only because דוד was still strong, so it was fear and not loyalty

steps.title: Another reason: דוד's fortune was still strong
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא offers a second answer to why יואב did not follow אבשלום: דוד's stars (his good fortune) were still standing strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: דוד's stars were still standing strong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question in step 15: why didn't יואב actually join אבשלום? רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says דוד's fortune was still strong, so יואב was afraid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said יואב held back because דוד himself was still physically strong. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא points to something else: דוד's luck and support were still in force. The next step backs this up by describing the loyal force around דוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Stars or astrologers; here it means a person's fortune or luck

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
David's stars were still standing,
phrases.notes: Literally "David's astrologers"; it means the stars that ruled his fortune were still on his side.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: עֲדַיִין אִיצְטַגְנִינֵי שֶׁל דָּוִד קַיָּימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question that רבי אלעזר answered in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why didn't יואב actually follow אבשלום?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דוד's fortune was still strong, so יואב was afraid to rebel.

steps.title: דוד's 400 loyal young fighters
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב describes 400 young men who were דוד's powerful enforcers. This shows how strong דוד's position still was.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: דוד had 400 young men. All were sons of יפת תואר women, they grew their hair in a special non-Jewish style, they walked at the head of the troops, and they were דוד's strongmen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא with a teaching about the elite force that protected דוד. With men like these around דוד, יואב did not dare rebel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement explains in practical terms what "דוד's stars were still standing" looked like. דוד had a loyal, powerful group of fighters. Rebelling against a king with such backing was too dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: A captive woman taken in war (דברים 21:10-14)
A non-Jewish hairstyle, with a lock of hair grown long

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת יְלָדִים הָיוּ לוֹ לְדָוִד,
phrases.english: David had four hundred young men,
phrases.notes: These are not his own children. They are young soldiers in his service.

phrases.english: all of them were sons of captive women,
and they grew a gentile-style lock of hair,
and they would walk at the head of the troops,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵן הֵן בַּעֲלֵי אֶגְרוֹפִין שֶׁל דָּוִד.
phrases.english: and they were David's strongmen.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 17 by describing the force behind דוד's strength.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד's power was still strong enough to scare יואב
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב, describing דוד's 400 elite young fighters

steps.title: דוד and יואב needed each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the negative picture of יואב disagrees with רבי אבא בר כהנא. He says that without דוד, יואב could not win wars, and without יואב, דוד could not learn תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי אבא בר כהנא, who said: If not for דוד, יואב could not have waged war. If not for יואב, דוד could not have learned תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different אמורא sees יואב in a positive light. In his view, יואב and דוד were partners who made each other successful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps describe יואב as someone who wanted to rebel against דוד. רבי אבא בר כהנא instead describes a loyal partnership: דוד's תורה brought success in battle, and יואב's fighting gave דוד the peace to learn. That view does not fit with יואב planning to betray דוד.
steps.confusionAlert: "ופליגא" does not mean רבי אבא בר כהנא is arguing about the 400 young men. It means his positive view of יואב clashes with the claim that יואב wanted to join אבשלום.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana,
phrases.notes: "This" means the idea from earlier that יואב wanted to rebel against דוד.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: אִילְמָלֵא דָּוִד לֹא עָשָׂה יוֹאָב מִלְחָמָה,
phrases.english: Were it not for David, Joab would not have waged war,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילְמָלֵא יוֹאָב לֹא עָסַק דָּוִד בַּתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and were it not for Joab, David would not have learned Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that a different view of יואב's character conflicts with the previous steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד and יואב depended on each other: דוד's תורה gave יואב success in war, and יואב's army gave דוד the peace to learn.

steps.title: The פסוק shows the partnership
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא proves his point from a פסוק that mentions דוד's justice and יואב's command of the army side by side. Each one made the other possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And דוד did justice and kindness for all his people, and יואב בן צרויה was over the army." Why could דוד do justice? Because יואב was over the army. And why could יואב be over the army? Because דוד did justice for all his people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי אבא בר כהנא. It reads the two halves of the פסוק as causing each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts דוד's justice and יואב's army command right next to each other. רבי אבא בר כהנא reads this placement as cause and effect running in both directions. Each half of the פסוק explains the other.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אבא בר כהנא, יואב was דוד's essential partner. דוד's תורה and יואב's battles held each other up.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי דָוִד עֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה לְכׇל עַמּוֹ
phrases.english: As it is written: "And David did justice and kindness for all his people,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 8:15-16

phrases.english: and Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army."

phrases.aramaic: מָה טַעַם ״דָוִד עֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה לְכׇל עַמּוֹ״?
phrases.english: What is the reason that "David did justice and kindness for all his people"?
Because "Joab was over the army."
And what is the reason that "Joab was over the army"?

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּ״דָוִד עֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה לְכׇל עַמּוֹ״.
phrases.english: Because "David did justice and kindness for all his people."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי דָוִד עֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה לְכׇל עַמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי אבא בר כהנא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That דוד and יואב depended on each other
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 8:15-16, which places דוד's justice right next to יואב's army command

steps.title: What does בור הסירה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק describing how יואב brought אבנר back from a place called בור הסירה, and asks what the name means.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And יואב went out from דוד and sent messengers after אבנר, and they brought him back from בור הסירה." What is בור הסירה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the יואב story: his killing of אבנר. It asks about the meaning of the strange place name בור הסירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name of the place seems unneeded, so the גמרא assumes it hints at something. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit or well; here, a hint to a water jug

phrases.english: "And Joab went out from David,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 3:26

phrases.english: and sent messengers after Abner,
and they brought him back from Bor Sirah."
What is "Bor Sirah"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״בּוֹר הַסִּירָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the יואב story: the death of אבנר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the name בור הסירה hint at?

steps.title: A pit and a thorn caused אבנר's death
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא explains that the name hints at a "pit" and a "thorn", two things that caused אבנר to be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא said: A pit and a thorn caused אבנר to be killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר כהנא answers that the name בור הסירה is a hint. Two things, a pit and a thorn, are what made אבנר deserve to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא splits the name into two words, בור and סירה. Each word points to an earlier event connected to אבנר. The name of the place where his death began reminds us why it happened.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹר וְסִירָה גָּרְמוּ לוֹ לְאַבְנֵר שֶׁיֵּהָרֵג.
phrases.english: A pit and a thorn caused Abner to be killed.
phrases.notes: This hints at שאול's water jug and cut robe. אבנר brushed them off instead of helping make peace between שאול and דוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹר וְסִירָה גָּרְמוּ לוֹ לְאַבְנֵר שֶׁיֵּהָרֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name hints at a pit and a thorn, which caused אבנר's death.

steps.title: יואב judged אבנר like a סנהדרין
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק saying יואב took אבנר into the gate, רבי יוחנן says יואב judged him according to the law of the סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And יואב took him aside into the gate to speak with him quietly." רבי יוחנן said: He judged him with the law of the סנהדרין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק, and רבי יוחנן explains that taking אבנר "into the gate" means יואב held a kind of trial. This sets up the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gate of the city was where courts sat. So רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as saying יואב did not just murder אבנר; he first put him through a legal hearing. The next steps show what that hearing sounded like.

keyTerms.meaning: The city gate, where the court would sit
The law of the סנהדרין, a court-style trial

phrases.english: "And Joab took him aside into the gate
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 3:27

phrases.english: to speak with him quietly."
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
That he judged him with the law of the Sanhedrin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁדָּנוֹ דִּין סַנְהֶדְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of אבנר's death with the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יואב put אבנר through a court-style trial before killing him.

steps.title: יואב asks: why did you kill עשאל?
steps.stepSummary: יואב opens the trial by asking אבנר why he killed עשאל, יואב's brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why did you kill עשאל?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first question of יואב's "trial." He demands that אבנר explain why he killed עשאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like a court, יואב first asks the accused to give his side. The whole hearing is about whether killing עשאל was allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא קְטַלְתֵּיהּ לַעֲשָׂאֵל?
phrases.english: He said to him: Why did you kill Asahel?
phrases.notes: "He" is יואב, speaking to אבנר. עשאל was יואב's brother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא קְטַלְתֵּיהּ לַעֲשָׂאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the trial that רבי יוחנן described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What justification did אבנר have for killing עשאל?

steps.title: אבנר: עשאל was a רודף
steps.stepSummary: אבנר answers that עשאל was chasing him to kill him. That made him a רודף, whom one may kill in self-defense.
steps.simpleTranslation: עשאל was a pursuer.
steps.whatsHappening: אבנר defends himself. He says that עשאל was a רודף, chasing him to kill him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the law of רודף, someone chasing another to kill him may be stopped, even by killing him. אבנר is claiming his act was legal self-defense.

keyTerms.meaning: A pursuer who is chasing someone to kill him

phrases.english: Asahel was a pursuer.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשָׂאֵל רוֹדֵף הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אבנר answers יואב's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עשאל was a רודף, so killing him was self-defense.

steps.title: You could have stopped him by hurting a limb
steps.stepSummary: יואב challenges אבנר: you should have saved yourself by wounding one of עשאל's limbs instead of killing him.
steps.simpleTranslation: You should have saved yourself by hitting one of his limbs!
steps.whatsHappening: יואב pushes back on אבנר's defense. Even if עשאל was a רודף, אבנר did not need to kill him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה is that if you can stop a רודף by wounding him, you may not kill him. יואב is saying that אבנר used more force than the law allows.

keyTerms.meaning: To save (yourself) from him, to stop him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key rule of רודף: you may only use as much force as you need. If wounding is enough, killing is forbidden.

phrases.english: You should have saved yourself by hitting one of his limbs!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה לְךָ לְהַצִּילוֹ בְּאֶחָד מֵאֵבָרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אבנר's רודף defense.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבנר's claim that killing עשאל was allowed because he was a רודף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a רודף can be stopped by wounding a limb, killing him is not allowed.

steps.title: אבנר: I couldn't aim that well
steps.stepSummary: אבנר answers that he was not able to aim precisely enough to hit only a limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: I wasn't able to do that to him.
steps.whatsHappening: אבנר defends himself again. He says he could not manage to hit just a limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבנר accepts the rule that wounding comes first. He claims that in his situation he simply could not do it, so killing was his only choice.

phrases.english: I was not able to do that to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא יְכֵילִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אבנר answers יואב's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual claim: wounding was not possible here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אבנר should have wounded עשאל instead of killing him
steps.terutzMaskana: אבנר says he could not aim at a limb, so killing was necessary

steps.title: You hit the fifth rib, yet couldn't hit a limb?
steps.stepSummary: יואב rejects אבנר's excuse. אבנר aimed exactly at the fifth rib, so he surely could have aimed at a limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, you were able to aim right at his fifth rib, and you couldn't aim at one of his limbs?
steps.whatsHappening: יואב knocks down אבנר's last excuse. The exact spot where אבנר struck עשאל proves he could aim well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבנר hit עשאל in a precise, deadly spot, the fifth rib. That shows he had full control of his aim. So he could have wounded a limb instead, and he is guilty for killing a רודף when it was not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The fifth rib, where עשאל was struck (שמואל ב 2:23)

steps.whatToRemember: In יואב's trial, אבנר's רודף defense failed. He showed he could aim exactly, so he should have wounded עשאל instead of killing him.

phrases.english: Now, you aimed at him in the fifth rib,
phrases.notes: See שמואל ב 2:23, where אבנר struck עשאל under the fifth rib.

phrases.english: and you could not hit him in one of his limbs?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא בְּדוֹפֶן חֲמִישִׁית כַּוֵּונְתְּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אבנר's answer in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבנר's claim that he could not aim at a limb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hitting the exact fifth rib shows precise aim, so he could have hit a limb too.

steps.title: יואב took אבנר aside by trickery
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the word בַּשֶּׁלִי means יואב spoke to אבנר with deception.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says יואב took אבנר aside 'to speak with him בַּשֶּׁלִי.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: this means by way of trickery.
steps.whatsHappening: The trial is over, and the גמרא now explains a word in the פסוק that describes how יואב got אבנר alone before killing him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rare word בַּשֶּׁלִי is read as connected to שָׁלוּ, trickery or deception. So the פסוק is telling us that יואב pretended to have a friendly talk, but really he was setting a trap.

keyTerms.meaning: A rare word in the פסוק, usually understood as 'quietly' or 'privately'

phrases.english: "To speak with him quietly"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 3:27. This is where יואב takes אבנר aside before killing him.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
By way of deception.
phrases.notes: רב hears the word בַּשֶּׁלִי as connected to שָׁלוּ, trickery.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדַבֵּר אִתּוֹ בַּשֶּׁלִי, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the trial dialogue ends, the גמרא turns to explaining words in the related פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בַּשֶּׁלִי means יואב spoke to אבנר with trickery.

steps.title: The חומש is the fifth rib
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that 'the חומש' means the fifth rib, where the gallbladder and liver hang.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'he struck him there in the חומש.' רבי יוחנן said: this means the fifth rib, the spot where the gallbladder and liver hang.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing with the same פסוק about יואב and אבנר, the גמרא explains the word חומש, the exact spot on the body where the blow landed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן gives the same explanation he gave in Step 7: the חומש is the fifth rib, a deadly spot where the gallbladder and liver hang. The same word חומש is used both for where אבנר struck עשאל and for where יואב struck אבנר.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the פסוק for a spot on the body, linked to the number five

phrases.english: "And he struck him there in the ḥomesh"
phrases.notes: The word שָׁם matches שמואל ב 3:27, where יואב strikes אבנר. The same word חֹמֶשׁ also shows up in 2:23 about עשאל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
In the fifth rib,
The place where the gallbladder and liver hang.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיַּכֵּהוּ שָׁם אֶל הַחֹמֶשׁ, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוקים of יואב killing אבנר after Step 29, using רבי יוחנן's fifth-rib reading also seen in Steps 7 and 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חומש means the fifth rib, where the gallbladder and liver hang.

steps.title: Why אבנר and עמשא were better and more righteous than יואב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains שלמה's words: אבנר and עמשא were 'better' in Torah learning and 'more righteous' in refusing to obey wrong orders.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'ה' will return his blood on his head, because he struck down two men more righteous and better than he.' 'Better': they would explain the words אך and רק as limits, and יואב did not. 'More righteous': they were ordered out loud and did not obey, but יואב was ordered only in a letter and he obeyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two words of praise, טובים and צדיקים, that שלמה used for אבנר and עמשא when comparing them to יואב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word gets its own meaning. 'Better' means greater in Torah: they read the limiting words אך and רק carefully. 'More righteous' means better in action: even a direct spoken order did not move them to kill, while יואב obeyed a mere letter and killed.

keyTerms.meaning: The limiting words אך and רק in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words. 'Better' (טובים) is about Torah learning, and 'more righteous' (צדיקים) is about what they actually did.

phrases.english: "And the Lord shall return his blood upon his own head
phrases.notes: מלכים א 2:32. שלמה is speaking about יואב.

phrases.english: for he fell upon two men
more righteous and better than he."
phrases.notes: The two men are אבנר and עמשא.

phrases.english: "Better" — for they would expound the words akh and rak,
phrases.notes: These limiting words were read as limits on how far a king's orders must be obeyed.

phrases.english: and he did not expound them.
"More righteous" — for they were ordered by mouth and did not do it,
phrases.notes: שאול told them out loud to kill the כהנים of נוב, and they refused.

phrases.english: while he was ordered in a letter and did it.
phrases.notes: דוד's letter about killing אוריה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵשִׁיב ה׳ אֶת דָּמוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ אֲשֶׁר פָּגַע בִּשְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים צַדִּקִים טוֹבִים מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the killings themselves to שלמה's judgment of יואב for those killings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבנר and עמשא were better in Torah and more righteous in deed than יואב.

steps.title: עמשא did not suspect יואב
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that עמשא did not guard himself from יואב's sword because he never suspected him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And עמשא did not guard himself from the sword in יואב's hand.' רב said: because he did not suspect him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why עמשא let himself be killed so easily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sword was right there in יואב's hand, so why did עמשא not protect himself? רב answers that עמשא simply never imagined יואב would murder him.

phrases.english: "But Amasa took no heed
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 20:10.

phrases.english: of the sword in Joab's hand."
Rav said: Because he did not suspect him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲמָשָׂא לֹא נִשְׁמַר בַּחֶרֶב אֲשֶׁר בְּיַד יוֹאָב, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with עמשא, the second of the two men named in Step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עמשא did not guard himself because he did not suspect יואב.

steps.title: Was יואב's house really a wilderness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק can say יואב was buried in his house 'in the wilderness.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he was buried in his house in the wilderness.' Was his house a wilderness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a strange phrase in the פסוק about יואב's burial and sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house is a lived-in place and a wilderness is empty, so calling a house a 'wilderness' does not fit. The question prepares the next steps, which read 'wilderness' as a description of the house.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a question of surprise)

phrases.english: "And he was buried in his own house, in the wilderness."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 2:34. This is about יואב.

phrases.english: Is that to say his house was a wilderness?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ בֵּיתוֹ מִדְבָּר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the killings to יואב's burial and his good qualities.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does it mean that יואב's house was 'in the wilderness'?

steps.title: יואב's house was open to everyone
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that יואב's house was 'like a wilderness': open to all, because he welcomed the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: it was like a wilderness. Just as a wilderness is open to everyone, so too יואב's house was open to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by reading 'wilderness' as a comparison: יואב's house was like a wilderness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody owns a wilderness, so anyone may enter. In the same way, יואב's door was open to all, and the poor came in freely. The פסוק is praising יואב's kindness.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Like the wilderness:
phrases.notes: רב reads בַּמִּדְבָּר, 'in the wilderness,' as if it said כַּמִּדְבָּר, 'like the wilderness.'

phrases.english: just as the wilderness is open to all,

phrases.aramaic: אַף בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל יוֹאָב מוּפְקָר לַכֹּל.
phrases.english: so too Joab's house was open to all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יואב's house was like a wilderness: open to all.

steps.title: יואב's house was clean of sin
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: like a wilderness, יואב's house was free of theft and forbidden relationships.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: it was like a wilderness. Just as a wilderness is clean of theft and forbidden relationships, so too יואב's house was clean of theft and forbidden relationships.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to understand the comparison to a wilderness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An empty wilderness has no people, so no one there steals or sins with forbidden relationships. יואב's house was just as clean of these sins. The first answer praised his kindness, and this one praises his purity.

phrases.english: Alternatively: like the wilderness:
just as the wilderness is clean of theft and sexual immorality,

phrases.aramaic: אַף בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל יוֹאָב מְנוּקֶּה מִגָּזֵל וַעֲרָיוֹת.
phrases.english: so too Joab's house was clean of theft and sexual immorality.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: כַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 33's question, alongside Step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יואב's house was like a wilderness: free of theft and forbidden relationships.

steps.title: יואב fed the poor even with treats
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that יואב 'kept the city alive' by feeding the poor generously, even giving them small fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And יואב kept alive the rest of the city.' רב יהודה said: he would even taste small fish and little salted fish and hand them out to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains one more פסוק praising יואב and ends this section on his good qualities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Kept the city alive' could mean only giving basic food. רב יהודה teaches that יואב went further and gave even small extra foods, so the poor would lack nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: Even though יואב killed אבנר and עמשא, who were better than him, the גמרא also praises him: his home was open to all, clean of sin, and he fed the poor generously.

phrases.english: "And Joab kept alive the rest of the city."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 11:8.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Even small fish and little salted fish
he would taste and hand out to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיוֹאָב יְחַיֶּה אֶת שְׁאָר הָעִיר, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another praise of יואב's generosity, building on Step 34's open house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יואב fed the poor generously, even giving them small fish.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק נגמר הדין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes פרק נגמר הדין with the traditional הדרן line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק נגמר הדין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has reached the end of the פרק, and this line formally closes it. There is no new argument here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן means 'we will return.' Learners say it to the פרק they just finished, like saying goodbye to a friend you plan to see again. It closes the long discussion of the court's final verdict and the order of executions.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. It is the formula said when finishing a פרק.
The verdict was concluded. These are the opening words and name of this פרק.
A chapter of the משנה and גמרא.

steps.whatToRemember: פרק נגמר הדין is now finished. It ended with אגדה about יואב: his death, his house being 'like a wilderness,' and his kindness to the poor.
steps.confusionAlert: The name נגמר הדין is not a halachic statement here. It is simply the title of the פרק, taken from its opening words.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
phrases.notes: This is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק, showing our wish to come back and learn it again.

phrases.english: [chapter] "The verdict was concluded"

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ נִגְמַר הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final אגדה about יואב in step 36.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The sixth פרק of סנהדרין, נגמר הדין, is complete.
